audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Olaf the first-item row and the two-item row, while whys[5] says 'it is even now' and whys[6] and late say Vladimir takes over. The packet flags the chart as contradicting a 47.01% win rate.
audit.why: Olaf's claim in this lane is entirely pre-item; handing him the late rows is what makes a sub-50% matchup read as won. Rows 0-4 belong to Olaf (Vladimir has no escape before Sanguine Pool, and it is 28s at rank 1), row 5 is even, row 6 is Vladimir's.
audit.corrected: Olaf rows 1 through 6, Skill at first item, Vladimir at two-plus items — matching the packet chart and the prose already on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text says Sanguine Pool as if it were a short-cooldown escape, and never gives the number.
audit.why: 28/25/22/19/16s is the single most exploitable fact in the lane — a maxed-out W is still 16s, and Olaf's Undertow is 9s with a full refund on pickup. That gap is the whole early game.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1; bait it and the next 20+ seconds are free.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'W-omnivamp healing you through his Q' — Riot's text for Olaf's W is attack speed and a shield; the life steal sits on the passive, Berserker Rage. Separately, nothing anywhere mentions Crimson Pact.
audit.why: Crimson Pact converts 30 bonus health into 1 AP, which is exactly why the 'Stack pure HP' don't exists — but the page never says so, leaving the advice unexplained. And the 2s of untargetability on pool is what blanks Reckless Swing, so E timing is the decisive interaction.
audit.corrected: W shields; the passive heals. Crimson Pact makes raw HP feed his AP — buy magic resist. Hold Reckless Swing until he surfaces from pool.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block carries no numbers at all.
audit.why: Pool 28s at rank 1, Tides of Blood 13s at rank 1, Hemoplague a flat 120s.
47.01% over 1270 games; once the chart stops awarding Olaf the item rows the page and the number agree.

notes: Whole chart proposed as one matched-pair group so the packet defect ('Olaf 5/7 stages on a 47% lane') is resolved in a single atomic change: Olaf owns the pre-item rows, Vladimir owns two-plus items. Minions blocking Tides of Blood comes straight from Riot's own description ('can be blocked by enemy units'). Whether Sanguine Pool's untargetability can dodge Reckless Swing mid-cast or only prevent the cast is not in the kit text — the copy was kept to the safe form, hold E until he surfaces.
